content.rationale: The release is now a local step over artifacts, not yaml a reader judges, so the gate is runnable rather than reviewed. The version decision (nlomlqum) records one token; the release's use of it is that a local entry point substitutes a named version for that token, driven by the recorded text, and then drives build, release and publish from the dist machinery (trolstmt's manifest is the surface the version lands on). tests/version_release/version_release_test.py reads the recorded token from nodes/nlomlqum.json and the platforms and installers from dist-workspace.toml, requires no file under .github/workflows/ because the decision removes the whole generated set, and then runs the entry point in throwaway copies of the tree with dist, cargo, git, jj, gh, curl and wget replaced by recording stubs: no build, no network, no repository touched. The copies differ only in what the record and the manifest carry, so the token has to be the thing the substitution follows. Success is observed once per documented interface form — the named version as a positional argument, as --version <v>, as --tag v<v>, as a bare v<v>, as VERSION=<v> in the environment, and on standard input, each form given its own distinct version — because the release node documents that a caller may name the version in any of those six forms and the gate holds the entry point to that documented interface: an entry point that accepts only one of them leaves a caller who names the version another way unreleased, so every form has to substitute on its own and each form that does not is named. It conforms when: the record holds T and the manifest carries T, and the manifest's [package] version becomes the requested version; a substituted record T' (not T) with the manifest carrying T' still becomes the requested version, so a literal built into the entry point does not satisfy it; the same tree asked for a second, different named version puts that second version in the manifest, so the version that lands is the one the caller names; the tree whose manifest already carries the requested version is released rather than refused — exit 0, dist untouched, and build, release and publish still driven — because the decision allows the substitution to be a no-op there and that is the only state that can release the current tree, and this is checked for each requested version so a no-op keyed to one literal value does not pass; a record holding T while the manifest carries a version the record does not carry and does not equal the request, and a missing record, each make the entry point exit non-zero, drive no dist and leave the manifest as it was, rather than overwrite a version the record does not name; the conforming run exits 0, since a non-zero exit is a failed release; the recorded dist invocations cover an actual build — `dist plan` plans a build and builds nothing and is not credited — plus a release step and a publish, driven in the order build, then release, then publish — the pair that is out of order is named — because a publish that runs before the build releases artifacts that were never built; with the `dist build` stub exiting non-zero the entry point exits non-zero and drives no later step, where stopping is observed as no build, release or publish invocation recorded after the failing one, rather than inferred; and dist-workspace.toml is byte-identical afterwards. One accepted form is reused to offer the second version, so the version that lands is the one the caller names rather than a literal the entry point carries. It needs no cargo build, no dist install and no network, tracks the recorded token and the recorded dist plan rather than the decision's wording, and requires no workflow and no CI call into the script, because the accepted consequence of this layer is that no CI remains.
